[quote=norrhollow;58819193]"About modest, all things considered." Almstedt coolly lamented. "Though not bad, I'm guessing it wasn't easy setting up shop in a place with uh... nasty acoustics..."

Almstedt looked at the walls of the training facility, then to the rack of revolutionary instruments, taking it all in. Though, as SummitONE's CEO, Almstedt's role was on the corporate side of things, not field work. For this, Almstedt turned to the two figures behind him, who had been quietly staring all around the place, seemingly in search of something.

"You two." Almstedt began. "Any grand opinions of our colleagues' faculties?"

The two SummitONE contractors looked at each other silently. Then, seemingly unprompted, one of them would take off their head coverings at last. Beneath the coverings was a young man, High Albic, likely in his later 20s or mid 30s, though with eyes that seemed over a decade older, and with silvering hair to match. Judging by his much heavier gear, he had to be a weapons specialist of sorts.

The contractor did not speak for a few seconds, instead taking a moment to breath in the stuffy air of the training grounds.

"Good day, Mr. Madhir. My name is Ulf Mayne, Commanding Officer and Regional Operations Manager of SummitONE Solutions Shamat and Team Leader for this operation" The man's voice was calm and monotonous, like a featureless and stony plain. "If I might give a comment... SummitONE Solutions has a large training facility in Stormhaven, which could be used as a template to renovate your current facilities. Notably, I'm seeing here a lack of hearing protection for your men, which would likely have some effect on their combat capabilities, no offense. We'll be able to provide bullet stopping, reinforced concrete, rubberized barriers, everything and anything to ensure that this place could be a safe and controlled environment for your forces."

As he was commenting, the other contractor would take off their head coverings as well. Surprisingly, she would be a woman, and out of respect for the Sal-Baliz she would only remove her goggles, keeping her helmet and mask to keep her hair from flowing out. Like Mayne, she was a pale-faced High Albic, also with almost silvery, but closer to brown hair, and deep amber eyes to match.

"Freya Moran, Deputy Operations Manager for SummitONE Solutions Shamat!" The woman loudly introduced herself, clearly the foil to Mayne's calm and collected personality. "These guns you're using too... they look like they're long overdue for maintenance, maybe we can set up ourselves some little factories here and there all over Sal-Baliz, managed and run by your own people, with materials sourcing straight out of the SummitONE inventory... y'know, so there's no risk of things blowing up when it matters the most?"

As the two contractors made their statements, Xavier Almstedt turned to the supreme leader to gauge his reaction.

"Not bad, huh? These two combined are some of the best that SummitONE Solutions has to offer. They've each served in dozens of international security contracts and domestic assignments, so they know what they're talkinga bout. What do you think, Mr. Mandhir?"[/quote]

"Well, let's get to it then, Mr. Mandhir." Almstedt would say, stuffing his hands into his pockets. His tone was light and easy, almost jovial. "First things first, SummitONE Solutions will be establishing an outpost on the coastline of West Shamat. We currently have a fleet of dark ships ready and waiting in the Baliwick to deliver all the resources you'll need. Concrete, steel, structural components, air ventilation systems, kevlar, rubber, coal... we'll even bring in engineers, since you'll need a lot more underground facilities."

Xavier Almstedt then walked away from the firing range and towards the exit of the facility, not to leave, but rather to get a good grasp of its structural integrity.

"... We can discuss pricing later, just know that we'll be offering very competitive rates here. You'll never see offerings like what SummitONE has ever again. By the end of the year, we'll make Sal-Baliz into a great power. So, what do you say Mr. Mandhir?"

[quote=shahzada;58820016][b]Question of the Day #78:[/b]

What role should education play in shaping a citizen?s political and ethical beliefs, and should there be limits on what can be taught in schools?

Nation Question: How would your nation handle this issue?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]
-
General Perspective:

Education plays a crucial role in shaping a citizens political and ethical beliefs by fostering critical thinking, civic responsibility, and moral reasoning. Schools should provide students with a broad and balanced education that encourages open inquiry, debate, and exposure to multiple perspectives rather than indoctrination. However, limits may be necessary to prevent the teaching of misinformation, extremism, or ideologically driven narratives that suppress independent thought.

Ormans Approach:

In the Emirate of the Sultanate of Orman, education is tightly regulated by the state to ensure alignment with national values, Islamic principles, and social stability while also promoting scientific and technological advancement.
		Civic & Political Education:
		Schools emphasize national identity, loyalty to the monarchy, and the responsibilities of citizenship.
		Political education is structured around Ormans governance model, focusing on the role of the monarchy, government institutions, and national unity.
		Debate and critical thinking are encouraged within the framework of national interests but radical or subversive ideologies are strictly prohibited.
		Ethical & Religious Education:
		Islamic ethics form the foundation of moral education, teaching virtues such as honesty, discipline, and respect for authority.
		Other worldviews may be studied in a controlled academic context, but Orman maintains Islam as the guiding moral framework.
		Limits on Education:
		Schools cannot promote ideologies that threaten national unity or contradict Islamic values.
		Western-style political activism, revolutionary ideologies, and divisive identity politics are restricted.
		Historical education is state-approved to ensure it aligns with Ormans official narrative and national pride.

In summary, Orman ensures education fosters national unity, strong ethical foundations, and technological progress while setting clear limits on content that could undermine social cohesion or state authority.
